matrix-specific character partitions for scapula and vertebrae are not tabulated in the DataCite metadata

datasets.name: Open Tree of Life synthetic tree (API)

checked.method: POST tree_of_life/about (synth_id opentree16.1, 1,931 source studies, 2,064 source trees, root 'cellular organisms' with 2,385,875 tips) and POST tnrs/match_names for Basilosaurus (ott 4942612) and Cetacea (ott 698424, infraorder); web page tree.opentreeoflife.org returned 503 on an earlier request

variables_present: a synthetic phylogeny over a very large taxon set; names Basilosaurus and Cetacea resolve in the taxonomy
variables_missing: whether Basilosaurus (extinct) is placed in the synthetic tree, as opposed to the taxonomy, was not queried
extinct archaeocetes have no molecular data, so any tree for them is itself morphology-based
the tree is not a character matrix, so character-level homoplasy cannot be computed from it
datasets.evidence: about response fields and match_names results as listed

summary: Cetacean morphological matrices exist on MorphoBank (42 DOIs including archaeocete projects) and a broad synthetic reference tree is available through the Open Tree API, but the matrices could not be opened (portal blocks scripted access) so separate scapular and vertebral character partitions are unconfirmed, and extinct archaeocetes have no molecular reference tree.
next_step: Download two or three cetacean matrices from MorphoBank in a browser, check whether characters are labelled by skeletal region, and decide the reference tree (molecular for extant cetaceans; published total-evidence tree for archaeocetes).
obstacles_confirmed: MorphoBank portal returned 403 to scripted requests, so matrices were not inspected.
No repository dataset tabulates homoplasy by skeletal region.
Zeuglodon-type fossils lack a molecular reference tree.
